profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
Senior Software Engineer at Google, and MIT graduate (BS CS '18, MEng CS/AI '19 @ MIT Media Lab).

Experience in R&D of AI systems, with heavy emphasis on machine learning. Includes work in computer vision, natural language processing/machine translation, and program synthesis.

positions.title: Machine Learning Research Assistant
positions.description:
AlterEgo, which I demoed at TED 2019, is a wearable device that aims to augment humans with the information and computational power of a computing device in a natural way. My research focused on creating a continuous “silent speech” recognition system that allows humans to converse covertly – without any speech or visible movement, instead with electric signals from the brain produced during subvocalization – with machines, artificial intelligent assistants, and other people.

Thesis: http://ericwadkins.com/thesis

Media Lab Profile: http://media.mit.edu/people/ewadkins

positions.title: MITRE Undergraduate Research and Innovation Scholar
positions.description: I led a year-long research project in the Quantum Photonics Group, sponsored by MITRE, that aimed to improve instrument localization and autonomous navigation. Prior work includes developing machine learning and computer vision-enabled algorithms to automate processes in the lab, such as detection and examination of microscopic-scale data near nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond.

positions.title: Machine Learning Intern
positions.description: I interned with NASA at the Goddard Space Flight Center, where I used machine learning to apply predictive models based on satellite measurements to applications of aerosol science. Specifically, my project focused on using data from the MODIS Terra and Aqua satellites and NASA's GEOS forecasting model to create a neural network model for the prediction of unknown atmospheric features around the world. The Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO) at NASA uses these features in global climate models to answer some of the fundamental questions of climate science.

company.name: NASA - National Aeronautics and Space Administration

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description: As an intern at Google’s Los Angeles office, my work included the design, implementation, testing, and concurrent optimization of an intelligent automated tool for YouTube’s infrastructure.

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description:
As an intern at Diameter Health, I developed full-stack applications and worked with proprietary algorithms that analyze data to reveal insights useful for healthcare organizations and clinicians. I’ve been heavily involved in the design, implementation, and testing of software.
---

Designed, implemented, and tested a free-text medication sig parser, using natural language processing (NLP) techniques such as tokenization and POS tagging, from data extraction to the end product.

Created scripts in Node.js to interface with database systems and automate the use of Diameter Health's other services.

Created a full-stack Return on Investment (ROI) tool for the Sales and Marketing division in order to increase sales and allow for the visualization of potential return on investment.

Continued work with Partners Healthcare on the research study initiated the previous year.

Worked towards setting up the company's IHE Profile to enable greater interoperability with other healthcare services.

Developed a full-stack application for Partners Healthcare as part of a research study to determine whether this automated predictive tool improves a clinician's ability to assess the risk of Chronic Kidney Disease.

Worked as part of a team developing an application to analyze the quality of Continuity of Care Documents (CCDs) to improve documentation for healthcare organizations.

Integrated feedback on applications tailored to the needs of individual organizations and provided technical assistance through calls and in-person meetings with clients.

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description: The InfoLab Group conducts research on artificial intelligence (AI), natural language processing (NLP) and multimedia information access, with the goal of bridging the gap between human and machine learning via computer-human interaction (CHI), as well as computer vision and machine learning methods. My work for the InfoLab Group focused on a video action recognition system capable of recognizing scenes based on the physical properties of the objects within them, providing a method of querying these scenes using natural language.

company.name: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL) InfoLab
